context: Camera/Composition Diversity Extension V1: SHINKAI_02 + MORI_04 additional real-frame sampling beyond the original 20/17 frames, following up on the prior Gap Assessment (22%/38% coverage) that concluded this was a real, solvable sampling gap, not a source limitation.
finding: Extracted and directly inspected 16 new real frames for SHINKAI_02 (12 usable after excluding 2 title cards, 1 UI/social-media screenshot insert, and 1 exact duplicate frame) and 15 new real frames for MORI_04 (all 15 usable), using the same ffmpeg scene-detection + single-frame-extract method as the original catalogs. Classified camera_distance for every new candidate against each catalog's own already-established vocabulary convention (e.g. MORI_04's own catalog already classifies tight single-face portraits as extreme-close, not close; SHINKAI_02's own catalog already classifies POV rain-blur and object inserts as extreme-close). Combined with the existing 13 (SHINKAI_02) and 14 (MORI_04) candidates: SHINKAI_02 maxRepeatedValueRatio(camera_distance) = 13/25 = 0.52 (extreme-close-dominant), MORI_04 = 15/29 = 0.517 (extreme-close-dominant). Both remain above the >0.5 fail threshold in validateGrammarCatalogSignal even after real, honest additional sampling using the source-material's own established labeling convention -- the bias narrowed slightly (from 0.538/0.643 originally) but did not cross the pass line for either source. This is consistent with a genuine stylistic property of both sources (Shinkai trailer: heavy use of extreme-close macro/POV inserts -- raindrops, screen taps, rings, guns, umbrella spokes; Mori apothecary short: heavy use of extreme-close insert-detail shots -- petals, scales, wax seals, cauldron steam, book pages) rather than a sampling artifact. Per explicit instruction not to force a pass by cherry-picking classifications or candidates, no edits were made to either exports/shinkai02-grammar-catalog.json or exports/mori04-grammar-catalog.json -- concluding CONCLUDED_LIMITATION for both, as-is.

context: Real Image Batch DNA Effect Verification V1: separating DNA-completeness vs. palette/geometry/scorer causes for SHINKAI_01/02 low camera_preservation in services/realImageBatchValidation.ts (the 10-scene real-image-batch-validation pipeline), and adding MORI_04 to its coverage.
finding: camera_preservation in scoreFromPixels() is computed as clampScore(min(horizontal_gradient/2.2, 48) + panEnergy*1200 + cameraEnergy*400 + 32), where panEnergy/cameraEnergy come directly from the UNFLOORED camera_velocity[0]/mean(camera_velocity) read from exports/source_video_dna/camera-behavior-dna/{SOURCE}.json. Checked all 8 batch sources (GHIBLI_01/02/03, SHINKAI_01/02, MORI_01/03, TITANIC_02): every one of their camera-behavior-dna files is the OLD synthetic hash-seeded placeholder schema (dna_id ending "-v2", no source/estimated_only/artifact_type fields) -- there is zero real-vs-synthetic DNA completeness variance to test in this dimension; all 8 are equally synthetic. SHINKAI_01/02 happen to have low seeded camera_velocity[0] values (0.0108/0.01) vs GHIBLI/MORI (~0.026-0.03). Critically, generateProductionPng() FLOORS the same value at 0.032 (effectivePan = max(abs(camVel), 0.032)) before it affects any actual generated pixel content -- so the generated images for ALL 8 sources use the identical 0.032 pan intensity (every source is below the floor). But scoreFromPixels() uses the raw, unfloored value directly as an additive score bonus with no corresponding floor, so SHINKAI scores ~20-25 points lower on the non-gradient term (~45-46 vs ~67-72 for GHIBLI/MORI) for a pixel difference that never actually occurred in the generated image. CONCLUSION: the SHINKAI camera_preservation gap is a scorer-formula floor-asymmetry artifact (generation floors at 0.032, scoring does not), NOT a DNA-completeness effect (no completeness variance exists to test) and NOT a palette/geometry effect (palette RGB and subject_bbox geometry play no role in this formula). The DNA-completeness-improves-generation-fidelity hypothesis is NOT_PROVEN for this metric -- correctly, per instruction, rather than forced. Did NOT touch the scoring formula/floor/thresholds (explicitly out of scope -- would be exactly the forbidden arbitrary score tuning). Separately: added MORI_04 to the batch by SWAPPING it for MORI_03 (not adding an 11th scene) after discovering the pipeline is a rigid, verify-script-enforced fixed-10 benchmark (images=10, ghibli=3/shinkai=2/mori=2/titanic=3 all hardcoded in scripts/verify-real-image-batch-validation.ts) -- appending a scene breaks that invariant and is not actually minimal. MORI_04 scored camera_preservation=100 (its real camera-behavior-dna seed value is in the same high range as MORI_01/03), independently corroborating the diagnosis. Also found MORI_04 already has 5x real coverage in the separate, larger, already-passing 100-scene batch (reports/real_image_batch_100_validation) -- the 10-scene batch was the only one actually missing it.
